description: Experimental L0/L1 synonym lexicon for NaVQA retrieval. It is used before graph/FAISS retrieval and never derived from gold answers.

source_evidence: Common English visual-object naming: couch, sofa, bench, and seating can describe the same answer target class in indoor seating contexts.
Common visual-language mismatch: large public art installations are often labeled as sculpture/statue/artwork in object descriptions.
Common vehicle naming: semi truck, tractor trailer, truck, trailer, and big rig can refer to overlapping heavy-vehicle targets.
Common vehicle naming: a van can be referred to as a minivan or delivery van in general visual descriptions.
Common text/OCR vocabulary: logo, sign, text, lettering, wordmark, and writing can all carry the asked visual text content.
Common street-view naming: a building name is often visible as a sign, storefront text, lettering, or business name.
Common street-scene naming: food trucks may be labeled as vendor trucks, concession trucks, trucks, or trailers.
Common spatial/event constraint naming: gate, entrance, entryway, gateway, and opening can describe the same passage constraint.
Common driving-scene naming: intersection, cross street, junction, and crossing are interchangeable spatial constraints.
Common street-scene naming: sidewalk can appear as walkway, pavement, curb, or pedestrian path in visual evidence.
Common building-object naming: door, doors, glass door, doorway, and entrance often describe related doorway objects.
Common clothing naming: jacket, coat, outerwear, top, and shirt can overlap in HSGG clothing descriptions.
Observed project evidence audit: HSGG/CG6 candidates contained cotton logo / cottoncomp text style descriptions around trailer objects.
Observed project evidence audit: HSGG candidates described the asked large art installation as metal sculpture/decorative sculpture.
Observed project evidence audit: HSGG candidates included Red couch / Red leather sofa / red bench for the couch target wording mismatch.
Observed project evidence audit: vehicle evidence can label the semi-truck target as yellow truck or yellow trailer.
Observed project evidence audit: street/building name questions may surface as sign text, storefront sign, or storefront lettering evidence.
